pages.lesson:
LESSON: READING 14.4.1 EXTENSIVE READING: SHORT STORY

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 14
Topic 14.4: Reading 14.4.1 Extensive reading: Short story

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 14.4.1 Extensive reading: Short story. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Where does a writer get what to write about?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the ideas in the short story
2. appreciate the value of short stories in reflecting social issues

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 14.4.1 EXTENSIVE READING: SHORT STORY
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 14.4.1 Extensive reading: Short story helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 14.4.1 EXTENSIVE READING: SHORT STORY
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify the ideas in the short story

What this means
In this part you learn to identify the ideas in the short story. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify the ideas in the short story.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 14.4.1 Extensive reading: Short story”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify the ideas in the short story. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Appreciate the value of short stories in reflecting social issues

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the value of short stories in reflecting social issues. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the value of short stories in reflecting social issues.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 14.4.1 Extensive reading: Short story to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the value of short stories in reflecting social issues. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 14.4.1 Extensive reading: Short story is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 14.4.1 Extensive reading: Short story”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify the ideas in the short story)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 14.4.1 Extensive reading: Short story to a partner. (skill: appreciate the value of short stories in reflecting social issues)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 14.4.1 Extensive reading: Short story to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify the ideas in the short story.
3. Practise this skill: appreciate the value of short stories in reflecting social issues.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 14.4.1 Extensive reading: Short story from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 14.4.1 Extensive reading: Short story: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Reading 14.4.1 Extensive reading: Short story?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Where does a writer get what to write about?
2. How are stories related to what happens in real life?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 14.4.1 Extensive reading: Short story means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify the ideas in the short story.
5. Be able to: appreciate the value of short stories in reflecting social issues.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
